questions.question: A thief is spotted by a constable from 200 m. When the constable starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the constable is 8 km/h and thief runs at the speed of 6 km/h, then how far (in m) will the thief be able to run before he is overtaken?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between constable and thief = 200 m

Speed of constable = 8 km/h

Speed of thief = 6 km/h

**Formula used:**

Distance = relative speed × time

**Calculation:**

Distance = relative speed × time

⇒ 200 = (8 - 6) × (5/18) × time

⇒ 200 = 2 × (5/18) × time

⇒ Time = (200 × 18)/10

⇒ Time = 360 sec

Distance covered by thief = 6 × (5/18) × 360

⇒ 6 × 100 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

​__**Concept:**__

• **Tissues **in plants are classified into two main groups, namely,** meristematic** and** permanent tissues** based on whether the cells being formed are capable of dividing or not.
 
• Further Permanent tissues are also categorised into 2 types -** Simple tissue **& **Complex tissue.**
 
• The** complex tissues **are made of more than one type of cells and these work together as a unit.
 
• **Xylem** and** phloem** constitute the complex tissues in plants.

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Xylem **functions as a conducting tissue for** water** and** minerals **from roots to the stem and leaves. It also provides mechanical strength to the plant parts.
 
• It is composed of four different kinds of elements, namely -** tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres**, and** xylem parenchyma.**
 
• **Tracheids** are elongated or **tube-like cells** with thick and lignified walls and tapering ends. These are dead and are without protoplasm.
 
• A** vessel** is a long cylindrical tube-like structure made up of many cells called** vessel members**, each with lignified walls and a large central cavity.
 
• The vessel cells are also devoid of protoplasm. Vessel members are interconnected through perforations in their common walls.
 
• **Xylem fibres **have highly thickened walls and obliterated central lumens. These may either be septate or aseptate.
 
• **Xylem parenchyma **cells are living and thin-walled, and their cell walls are made up of cellulose.

questions.question: If (x + y) : (y + z) : (z + x) = 11 : 13 : 16, and x + y + z = 200, then find the value of z.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of ratio parts = 11 + 13 + 16 = 40 units

This sum represents 2 × (x + y + z) = 2 × 200 = 400

1 unit = 400 ÷ 40 = 10

Value of (x + y) = 11 units = 11 × 10 = 110

Value of z = (x + y + z) − (x + y) = 200 − 110 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(x + y) : (y + z) : (z + x) = 11 : 13 : 16

Total sum x + y + z = 200

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33730484ad4074e2195338e7e2b95614870f61ba1e410f1b3d3ac6e68a1d51e8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let (x + y) = 11k, (y + z) = 13k, and (z + x) = 16k

⇒ (x + y) + (y + z) + (z + x) = 11k + 13k + 16k

⇒ 2(x + y + z) = 40k

⇒ 2(200) = 40k

⇒ 400 = 40k

⇒ k = 400 ÷ 40 = 10

⇒ x + y = 11k = 11 × 10 = 110

⇒ z = (x + y + z) − (x + y)

⇒ z = 200 − 110 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Sum Property

When cyclic sums like (a+b), (b+c), and (c+a) are given in a ratio, the sum of the ratio parts always equals 2 × (a+b+c).

Finding Individual Variables

To find variable z, subtract the pair (x + y) from the total (x + y + z). Similarly, x = Total − (y + z) and y = Total − (z + x).

Ratio Constant (k)

The constant k is the proportionality factor that converts ratio units into actual numerical values based on the given constraints.

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 144. If one of the numbers is 48, then what will be the difference of these two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know the rule: First Number × Second Number = HCF × LCM

Second Number = (12 × 144) ÷ 48

Second Number = 1728 ÷ 48 = 36

Difference between the numbers = 48 − 36 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

HCF of two numbers = 12

LCM of two numbers = 144

First number = 48

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = Product of their HCF and LCM

First number × Second number = HCF × LCM

**Calculations:**

⇒ 48 × Second number = 12 × 144

⇒ 48 × Second number = 1728

⇒ Second number = 1728 ÷ 48

⇒ Second number = 36

⇒ Difference of the numbers = First number − Second number

⇒ Difference = 48 − 36

⇒ Difference = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, their product is exactly equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. Formula: a × b = HCF × LCM. Note that this rule applies exclusively to two numbers, not three or more.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators). Similarly, LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).

Co-prime Numbers Property

If two numbers are co-prime (having no common factor other than 1), their HCF is always 1, and their LCM is strictly equal to their product.

questions.question: A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 900 in 2 years and Rs. 1080 in 5 years at simple interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 3 years (5 − 2) = Rs. 1080 − Rs. 900 = Rs. 180.

Interest for 1 year = Rs. 180 ÷ 3 = Rs. 60.

**Principal (P)** = Amount after 2 years − (2 × Interest per year) = 900 − 120 = Rs. 780.

**Rate (R)** = (Interest per year ÷ Principal) × 100 = (60 ÷ 780) × 100 = 7.69%.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.69 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Amount after 2 years (A₂) = Rs. 900, Amount after 5 years (A₅) = Rs. 1080.

**Formula Used:** Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; Amount (A) = Principal (P) + SI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f4ff6a83309e84d2bbbf81a8ee963c0ff0b1edfc9a37690afc4a394bcfd8258.png] 

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 3 years = Rs. 1080 − Rs. 900 = Rs. 180

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 1 year = 180 ÷ 3 = Rs. 60

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 2 years = 60 × 2 = Rs. 120

⇒ **Principal (P)** = Amount₂ − SI₂ = 900 − 120 = Rs. 780

⇒ **Annual Rate (R)** = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

⇒ R = (60 × 100) ÷ (780 × 1) = 100 ÷ 13

⇒ R ≈ 7.6923%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.69 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Calculation of Rate

Rate (R) can be calculated using 100 × Interest ÷ (Principal × Time). Always ensure the interest and time period correspond to each other.

Nature of Simple Interest

questions.question: Volume of mixture of milk and water is 60 litres which contains 10% water. How much water should be added to it so that % of water become 25% ?

__Shortcut Trick__

When only water is added, the absolute quantity of milk remains constant.

Initial Milk = Final Milk

90% of 60 = 75% of (60 + x) [Since final mixture has 25% water, milk is 75%]

54 = (75 ÷ 100) × (60 + x)

60 + x = 54 × (4 ÷ 3) = 72 ⇒ x = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12 litres.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Total volume of mixture = 60 litres

⇒ Initial water percentage = 10%

⇒ Final water percentage required = 25%

**Formula Used:**

⇒ By Alligation Method, Ratio = (Dearer % − Mean %) : (Mean % − Cheaper %)

⇒ Here, 5 units represent the original volume of 60 litres.

⇒ 1 unit = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 litres

⇒ Therefore, quantity of pure water to be added = 1 unit = 12 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 litres.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alligation Rule

Used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at their respective percentages must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired percentage. Ratio = (Dearer − Mean) : (Mean − Cheaper).

Constant Quantity Concept

When only one component (like water) is added to or removed from a mixture, the absolute quantity of the other component (like milk) remains unchanged. Equating initial and final quantities provides a quick one-step solution.

Successive Replacement Formula

questions.question: Sony and Mary can complete a painting in 4 days and 6 days, respectively. Then work on same painting on alternate days starting with Mary. In how many days will they together complete the painting?

**Total Work** (LCM of 4 and 6) = 12 units.

**Efficiency**: **Sony** = 3, **Mary** = 2.

In 2 days (Mary + Sony): 2 + 3 = 5 units.

In 4 days: 5 × 2 = 10 units. Remaining: 12 − 10 = 2 units.

Day 5: **Mary** completes remaining 2 units (2 ÷ 2 = 1 day).

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **Sony** = 4 days; Time taken by **Mary** = 6 days.

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **Sony** 4 12 3
 **Mary** 6 2

⇒ Total work = LCM(4, 6) = 12 units.

⇒ **Mary** starts on Day 1: Work done = 2 units.

⇒ **Sony** works on Day 2: Work done = 3 units.

⇒ Total work in 1 cycle (2 days) = 2 + 3 = 5 units.

⇒ Number of complete cycles = 12 ÷ 5 = 2 cycles (with remainder).

⇒ Work done in 2 cycles (4 days) = 2 × 5 = 10 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 12 − 10 = 2 units.

⇒ On Day 5, it is **Mary**'s turn. Time taken for remaining work = 2 ÷ 2 = 1 day.

⇒ Total time = 4 + 1 = 5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

Alternate Day Concept

questions.question: If the income of A is 50% less than the income of B, then B's income is what percent more than the income of A?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If **A** is 50% less than **B**, then the **ratio** of A : B = 50 : 100 = 1 : 2.

B is 1 unit more than A (since 2 − 1 = 1).

Percentage more = (Difference ÷ **Base Value A**) × 100

Percentage more = (1 ÷ 1) × 100 = 100%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Income of A is 50% less than income of B.

**Formula Used:** Percentage more = [R ÷ (100 − R)] × 100, where R is the **percentage decrease**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/01a304800509903bc752afc92a5a174fb85942a439144430dd0db22a31299ead.png] 

⇒ Let **Income of B** = 100

⇒ **Income of A** = 100 − 50% of 100 = 100 − 50 = 50

⇒ Difference = B − A = 100 − 50 = 50

⇒ **Percent more** = (Difference ÷ Income of A) × 100

⇒ Percent more = (50 ÷ 50) × 100

⇒ Percent more = 100%

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Percentage Relationship

If A is x% more than B, then B is [x ÷ (100 + x)] × 100% less than A.

Base Value Rule

The **percentage change** always depends on the **denominator (base value)**; when comparing how much more B is than A, A becomes the base value.

Successive Percentage

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective change is [a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100]%.</p

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 150 is divided into two parts. The first part is Rs. 2 more than three times the second part. Find the second part.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Subtract the excess amount from the **Total Sum**: 150 − 2 = 148.

The first part is now exactly 3 times the second part, creating a ratio of 3 : 1.

Total ratio parts = 3 + 1 = 4 units.

4 units = 148 ⇒ 1 unit = 148 ÷ 4 = 37.

Since the **Second Part** represents 1 unit, its value is 37.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 37.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Total Sum** = Rs. 150

Relation: **First Part** = 3 × **Second Part** + 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ddbc6bd00be5e467d271974f1a71bc918a614f2779c90e5928c8e7021fee53e.png] 

Let the **Second Part** be x.

Then, the **First Part** = 3x + 2.

⇒ First Part + Second Part = Total Sum

⇒ (3x + 2) + x = 150

⇒ 4x + 2 = 150

⇒ 4x = 150 − 2

⇒ 4x = 148

⇒ x = 148 ÷ 4

⇒ x = 37

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 37.**

**__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in One Variable

Equations of the form ax + b = c are used to find unknown quantities by isolating the variable using inverse operations.

Sum of Parts Rule

When a quantity is divided into multiple components, the arithmetic sum of all parts must always equal the original whole value.

Verification Technique

Always verify the answer by checking if the first part (3 × 37 + 2 = 113) and the second part (37) add up to the total sum (113 + 37 = 150).</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the successive percentage ratio multiplier method:

Final Price = Initial Price × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100

15288 = CP × (112 ÷ 100) × (91 ÷ 100)

CP = 15288 × (100 ÷ 112) × (100 ÷ 91) = 15000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Profit percentage for A = 12%

⇒ Loss percentage for B = 9%

⇒ Final price paid by C = ₹15,288

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Final SP = Initial CP × (100 ± Change%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22f05fbfc088bfacaa6a741f8ef652be267e4102c707efab18fb50dca0b42fe8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial cost price for A be ₹x.

⇒ Cost price for B = x × (100 + 12) ÷ 100 = 1.12x

⇒ Cost price for C = 1.12x × (100 − 9) ÷ 100

⇒ Cost price for C = 1.12x × 0.91 = 1.0192x

⇒ We know C pays ₹15,288. Equating the values:

⇒ 1.0192x = 15288

⇒ x = 15288 ÷ 1.0192 = 15000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value goes through sequential percentage changes, the equivalent net change can be found using the formula: a + b + (a × b ÷ 100), taking profit as positive and loss as negative.

Chain System in Transactions

In a sequential chain of sales, the Selling Price (SP) for the seller automatically becomes the Cost Price (CP) for the next buyer. The successive multiplier method is the fastest way to compute final values.

Profit & Loss Basics

Profit and loss are always calculated on the base Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise. Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 and SP = CP × (100 − L%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: The income of A is 25% less than the income of B whose income is 40% more than that of C. The income of C is 20% less than that of D. By what percent is the income of A more than the income of C?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Income A : Income B** = 75 : 100 = 3 : 4

Ratio of **Income B : Income C** = 140 : 100 = 7 : 5

Combined Ratio **A : C** = (3 × 7) : (4 × 5) = 21 : 20

**Percentage Increase** = ((21 − 20) ÷ 20) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income of **A** = 25% less than **B**

Income of **B** = 40% more than **C**

Income of **C** = 20% less than **D**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1e24c41fb71c3bc14ef3a1bacaffc338c37b4004fd286091553857b8a69ee6a5.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ Let the **Income of C** = 100

⇒ **Income of B** = 100 + (40% of 100) = 100 + 40 = 140

⇒ **Income of A** = 140 − (25% of 140) = 140 − (1/4 × 140)

⇒ **Income of A** = 140 − 35 = 105

⇒ Difference between **Income A** and **Income C** = 105 − 100 = 5

⇒ **Percentage Increase** = (Difference ÷ Income of C) × 100

⇒ **Percentage Increase** = (5 ÷ 100) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Comparison Formula

To find how much percent x is more than y, use: Percentage = ((x − y) ÷ y) × 100.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net change is (a + b + (ab ÷ 100))%. Note that a or b are negative for a decrease.

Fractional Equivalents

25% = 1/4 | 40% = 2/5 | 20% = 1/5. Using fractions simplifies complex calculations in ratio-based problems.</p

questions.question: From the top of a 72 meter high building the angle of depression of the top and bottom of a temple are observed to be 30º and 60º respectively. What is the height of the temple?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Height of the building = 72 meters

Angle of depression to the top of the temple = 30º

Angle of depression to the bottom of the temple = 60º

**Formula Used:**

 tan(theta) = frac{{Opposite}}{{Adjacent}} 

**Calculation:**

Let the height of the temple be h meters and the distance from the building to the temple be d meters.

For the top of the temple:

 tan(30^circ) = (72 - h)/(d) 

 tan(30^circ) = (1)/(sqrt{3)} 

⇒ (1)/(sqrt{3)} = (72 - h)/(d) 

⇒ d = sqrt{3} (72 - h) 

For the bottom of the temple:

 tan(60^circ) = (72)/(d) 

 tan(60^circ) = sqrt{3} 

⇒ sqrt{3} = (72)/(d) 

⇒ d = (72)/(sqrt{3)} 

⇒ d = 24 sqrt{3} 

Equating both expressions for d:

 sqrt{3} (72 - h) = 24sqrt{3} 

⇒ 72 - h = 24

⇒ h = 72 - 24

⇒ h = 48 meters

**The height of the temple is 48 meters.**

questions.question: What disease is caused by insulin deficiency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Diabetes Mellitus.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• Insulin is a type of **Peptide hormone.**
 
• It is produced by the beta cells of the **pancreatic islets.**
 
• The hormone is recognized as the **main anabolic hormone of the body.**
 
• It is responsible to regulate the metabolism of **carbohydrates, fats, and protein.​**

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diabetes mellitus** is a metabolic disease that causes **high blood sugar.**
 
• The insulin moves sugar from the blood cells into the other cells and used it as a form of energy.
 
• Diabetic patient doesn't make enough insulin or can't effectively use the insulin it does make.
 
• **Some of the important types of diabetes include -**

 
• Autoimmune diabetes
 
• Prediabetes
 
• Gestational diabetes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Diabetes insipidus (DI) and Diabetes mellitus (DM) are conditions characterized by abnormal regulation of fluids and sugars in the body, but they have different causes, symptoms, and treatments.

 
• Diabetes Insipidus (DI) is caused by deficiency of ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone).
 
• DI is primarily caused by a deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH), also known as vasopressin. ADH is responsible for regulating the balance of water in the body.

Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is caused by Insufficient Insulin or Insulin Ineffectiveness: DM is characterized by insufficient insulin production (Type 1 DM) or ineffective use of insulin by the body's cells (Type 2 DM).

 
• Type 1 Diabetes: Results from the immune system destroying insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas.
 
• Type 2 Diabetes: Develops when the body's cells become resistant to insulin or when the pancreas fails to produce enough insulin.

Key Differences:-

a)Hormonal Involvement:-

 
• DI: Involves a deficiency of ADH.
 
• DM: Involves insufficient insulin or insulin ineffectiveness.

b)Urine Characteristics:-

 
• DI: Results in dilute urine.
 
• DM: Causes the presence of glucose in the urine.

questions.question: The Weight of an object on Earth is 600 N. What will be its weight on moon?
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Acceleration due to gravity: The acceleration achieved by any object due to the gravitational force of attraction by any planet is called acceleration due to gravity by the earth.

 
 
• As each planet has a different mass and radius so the acceleration due to gravity will be different for a different planet.
 
 
 
• Weight: The weight(w) of an object is the force of gravity on the object and may be defined as the mass(m) times the acceleration of gravity(g).
 
 
• Weight is a force, the SI unit of weight is Newton.
 
 

Weight (W) = m g

Where m is mass and g is the acceleration due to gravity.

 
• Mass of the moon is 1/100 times and the radius of the moon is 1/4 times that of the earth.
 
• Since the acceleration due to the gravity of the moon is one-sixth of that of the earth.
 
• So Weight of any object on Moon = 1/6 × Weight of any object on the Earth surface.

EXPLANATION__:

Given that:

The weight of any object is **60**0 N in an earth surface

 The weight of the object on Moon = 1/6 × Weight of any object on the Earth surface = 600 × 1/6 = 100 N

questions.question: When was the Retired Sportsperson Empowerment Training (RESET) Programme officially launched by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2024**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Retired Sportsperson Empowerment Training (RESET) Programme** was officially launched by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** in the year **2024**.
 
• The programme aims to provide support, skill development, and empowerment to **retired sportspersons** transitioning to non-sporting careers.
 
• The **RESET Programme** focuses on equipping retired athletes with **, entrepreneurial training**, and **career counseling**.
 
• This initiative is part of the government's broader efforts to ensure the **welfare and rehabilitation** of sportspersons after their athletic careers.
 
• The programme emphasizes **mental health support** and the importance of financial literacy to help retired athletes manage their resources effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objectives of RESET Programme:**

 
 
• The programme aims to address the challenges faced by retired athletes, such as **loss of income**, **identity crisis**, and lack of career opportunities outside sports.
 
• It seeks to create a structured framework for **post-retirement career development** and **financial independence**.
 
• The initiative includes collaboration with **educational institutions** and **corporate sectors** to ensure job placements and skill development.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• The programme is open to athletes who have officially retired from professional sports and represented India in national or international events.
 
• Participants must register through the **official portal** provided by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
 
 
• **Skill Development Focus:**
 
 
• The RESET Programme provides training in areas such as **management**, **public relations**, **entrepreneurship**, and **technical skills**.
 
• Workshops and seminars are conducted to enhance **interpersonal skills** and **team leadership**.
 
 
 
• **Similar Initiatives:**
 
 
• In 2021, the government launched the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**, aimed at assisting athletes during their active careers. RESET extends this support post-retirement.
 
• The **Fit India Movement** also promotes overall physical and mental well-being, complementing the objectives of RESET.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The programme is implemented by the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** in collaboration with various **stakeholders**.
 
• Monitoring and evaluation mechanisms are in place to ensure the effectiveness of training and career assistance.

questions.question: In which year was the Indian National Congress formed?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Congress was founded on 28 December 1885.__
 
• The Indian National Congress was founded by A.O Hume who was Member of Imperial Civil Service and a noted political reformer, ornithologist, and botanist who worked in British India.
 
• He was sometimes referred to as Pope of Indian ornithology as he built up a personal collection of bird specimens as well as wrote extensively on his own observation as well as critical reviews of all the ornithological works of the time.
 
• The Indian National Congress which was established by A.O Hume had Womesh Chandra Banerjee as the first president of Congress and the first meeting was held in Bombay in December 1885.
 
• Lord Dufferin was the viceroy of India when the Indian National Congress was formed.
